dossiers.title: The Talos Principle
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: In self-contained first-person chambers, players route laser beams, reposition jammers and boxes, manipulate recordings and collect sigil pieces to unlock later zones.
Mechanics are introduced gradually and recombined across many puzzles; stars and secret routes demand especially inventive solutions, rewarding careful observation.
Open hub areas link puzzle chambers in classical ruins and later environments; optional terminals and secrets build toward multiple narrative conclusions.
Questions of personhood, artificial intelligence, obedience and what survives civilization are told through recorded fragments, terminals and a commanding unseen voice.
The atmospheric music, distinct outdoor architecture and contrast with tightly designed indoor puzzles make the reflective journey memorable.
Players split over the substantial puzzle count: some find ingenious variation through to the ending, others experience the latter half as repetitive and overlong.
Puzzle searching can become frustrating when secrets rely on hard-to-spot openings, exact item placement or lengthy detours instead of a new deductive insight.
The exploration and optional philosophical reading are slow and contemplative rather than action-forward, though narrative material can be bypassed by puzzle-focused players.
Some find the central philosophy compelling, while others view the treatment as shallow or its choice dialogues as insufficiently responsive to genuine debate.

Russian-language players praise the philosophical dialogue and narrative readability; the official product offers Russian interface, voice and subtitles, without a reported recurring translation defect.

conflicts.statement: For enthusiasts the long series of puzzles remains freshly demanding, while critics say later trials extend playtime without introducing enough new ideas.
Players disagree whether the philosophical story rewards reflection or only lightly sketches its themes behind conventional logic puzzles.

dossiers.title: My Furry Protogen 2 🐾
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 7 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: This short story-led visual novel continues the protagonists' relationship and search for an enemy across new planets; it presumes knowledge of the first installment.
Fans of the first entry often value Juno's caring relationship with the protagonist and the sequel's more serious emotional developments.
The compact, largely linear presentation suits a single extended reading session, though some player reactions want more depth around late plot turns.
One detailed player questions the protagonist's inconsistent behavior and an underexplained antagonist introduction, despite appreciating the relationship disagreements.
New character artwork and the futuristic setting are viewed positively by returning fans; the appeal depends heavily on attachment to this continuing cast.
Reported play is primarily reading a fixed visual-novel narrative rather than skill-based combat, puzzles or extensive branching; a small amount of choice and interactivity is secondary.

Russian participants in the exact game's community requested and discussed a fan translation shortly after release; this does not guarantee a supported official translation or that an unofficial patch remains usable.

conflicts.statement: The short fixed sequel satisfies some fans invested in Juno but others criticize character choices and want more narrative development.

dossiers.title: Sex, Please
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: This very short first-person adult-oriented psychological horror game combines wandering, interactions, surreal sequences and rudimentary puzzles rather than a conventional relationship simulator.
The deliberately provocative mixture of mature material, grotesque horror and absurdist presentation surprises players who initially expect a simple adult-themed experience.
At least one 2026 player reports finishing in under an hour, so the experience may feel like a compact spectacle rather than a substantial campaign.
A post-release Steam discussion describes difficulty knowing how to continue after a specific first-person escape sequence, consistent with occasionally opaque progression cues.
Audience reaction is sharply divided: some praise the bizarre spectacle or dark-horror surprise while others report strong discomfort and cannot enjoy its tone.
The combination of an unsettling narrative and a few puzzle or maze segments was unexpected enough for one player to view it as an actual horror game with a story.

A 2024 Russian demo discussion noted that some notes remained English when Russian was selected; this is strictly a pre-release demo report and does not establish localization flaws in the shipped game.
Early demo reactions also show substantial expectation mismatch between adult entertainment and horror presentation, but they are not evidence that all release players share those views.

conflicts.statement: Some appreciate the deliberate boundary-pushing horror experiment while others reject the disturbing subject matter and tone.
